meta.status: priest-confirmed corpora, hand-encoded; the encoded rules still need the same dual-competence reviewer's sign-off before ship (Part C standing caution)
invariants: The two corpora are separate bodies of law — never cross-wire days, binding ages, or rank-lift thresholds between OF and EF.
The calendar is imported (Introibo day-facts), never re-derived: the resolver computes no dates, ranks, or transfers.
Vigils omitted from the 1962 calendar (Immaculate Conception, All Saints) are modeled as ABSENT, not as days with a `none` obligation.
Unauthored countries fall back to universal law, never silently to US.

open_items.note: What does and does not break the penitential fast must be written into the corpus and priest-confirmed; the training guidance cross-links to it and currently dangles.
Lenten weekday partial-abstinence pattern (B5) flagged for primary-source confirmation at encode-review.
Exact Lenten Sunday/feast-of-precept interaction (B9) flagged for primary-source confirmation at encode-review.
Vigil of the Assumption is a retained fast-day vigil; its abstinence status is open until pinned against Introibo's 1962 calendar.

obligation_kinds.fast: One full meal plus smaller meals per the discipline's definition (OF: two smaller that together don't equal a full one; EF: a small morning and evening collation per approved local custom; meat and fish may be taken at the same meal under EF).
obligation_kinds.abstinence_of: OF abstinence: no flesh meat that day.
obligation_kinds.complete_abstinence_ef: EF complete abstinence: no flesh meat and no meat broth/soup; eggs, milk products, and condiments/seasonings even from animal fat are permitted.
obligation_kinds.partial_abstinence_ef: EF partial abstinence: meat permitted, but only at the one principal meal of the day.
obligation_kinds.penance_or_abstinence: Friday remains penitential; abstinence from meat has first place, and (US norm, c. 1253) another act of penance or work of charity may be substituted.

of.name: Ordinary Form — current discipline (1983 Code + USCCB)

rank_lift.rule: A solemnity falling on a Friday lifts the Friday abstinence (c. 1251). The solemnity list comes from the imported calendar, never re-derived.

recommendation.note: USCCB recommends continuing the fast to the Easter Vigil — a recommendation, not an added obligation; must never surface as binding.

rules.product_note: The app states the practice — Friday is penitential, abstinence has first place, substitution is permitted — and does not pronounce on whether omitting it is sinful. Gravity belongs to pastor/confessor (Part 2 §3 boundary).

fast.note: Universal 1962 law: completed 21st year. US particular law lowered this to 18. Scope-gated with the Ember Wed/Sat rule — the two must move together (B10, Part C #1).

rank_lift.rule: A Sunday or feast of precept lifts the abstinence/fast of a coinciding penitential day — EXCEPT during Lent, where the penance stands. Narrower than, and never to be confused with, the OF solemnity threshold.

rules.lift_note: Lifts only outside Lent, and only for a feast of precept / Sunday (B9).

rules.note: Ember Wed/Sat partial abstinence is the 1949 US modification; older universal practice was complete abstinence on all Ember days. Label as US norm in-app. Dates of all four sets come from the imported calendar.

rules.omitted_vigils_note: Immaculate Conception and All Saints vigils were omitted from the 1962 calendar itself — model as absent, never as `none`-obligation days.

universal.name: Universal law
universal.note: Fallback for unauthored countries — shown with: 'your country's bishops may specify differently — check with your parish.' Never silently serve US rules to a non-US user.

norm_profiles.selection: Onboarding captures a home country selecting ONE norm profile carrying all country-dependent values together — never separate toggles. Home country, not live location; the engine does not auto-switch when a user travels.
